correctness.rationale: For circular ternary words, conservation at each symbol implies exactly one common signed difference among the three opposite ordered-transition pairs. Strict ranking forces a nonzero difference. Every positive balance solution on six arcs is a strongly connected Eulerian multigraph and hence a cyclic word. The five and only five possible Dyck interleavings impose explicit necessary and sufficient strict inequalities in the positive integer gap parameters; minimizing n=6a+4p+2q+3d gives exactly 21,26,22,27,21. There are two cyclic directions and 3! orders per type, and the symmetry action is free. Distinct exact enumerations over 21,600 short integer profiles and over the integer parameter system agreed on all 60 minimum lengths. Every generated shortest-word witness was checked directly against its circular frequencies. The all-length proof uses the interleaving inequalities rather than empirical extrapolation.

value.rationale: In homopolymer-free cyclic ternary rank-modulation, sixty feasible rank-message orders are already deducible from existing unrestricted counts, but encoding them at minimum length was not quantified by those results. The exact lengths 21,22,26,27, with twelve worst-case message ranks requiring 27 positions, provide an optimal realizability budget and an exact design benchmark. The proof identifies structural bottlenecks in interleaving positive integer flow levels, not merely another count of already known ranks. This supplies a motivated sharp finite-alphabet result.
